analysis.investment_thesis: CP PLUS holds a dominant brand position in India's surveillance market with 20% revenue CAGR, but the stock is priced at 105x earnings that are massively inflated by a one-time INR 259 Cr "Other Income" in FY25 — strip that out and the core business earns ~90-100 Cr. At EV/EBITDA of 69x on genuine operating earnings, you're paying a spectacular price for a hardware distribution business with near-zero free cash flow.
key_strengths: India's leading CCTV/surveillance brand with 20.2% revenue CAGR (FY20-25) and expanding operating margins from 4.6% → 11.2%
Nearly debt-free with D/E of 0.08 and borrowings slashed from INR 436 Cr (FY24) to INR 128 Cr (FY25)
Government/infra surveillance tailwind with AI-IoT overlay (OnVigil) adding potential recurring revenue stickiness
key_risks: Catastrophic FCF conversion — reported INR 351 Cr net profit in FY25 yielded only INR 1 Cr FCF; FY24 showed INR 115 Cr profit with INR -187 Cr FCF — the working capital trap is structural
INR 259 Cr Other Income in FY25 (vs -12 Cr FY24) accounts for ~74% of reported net profit; forward estimates built on this base are fiction
Hardware distribution model facing relentless Chinese commoditization — they even distribute Dahua (competitor) products, signaling weak proprietary moat
red_flags: FY25 FCF/Net Income = 0.3% (INR 1 Cr FCF on INR 351 Cr profit) — textbook earnings quality failure
Other Income of INR 259 Cr in FY25 is almost certainly non-recurring; the 83% net profit CAGR headline is deeply misleading
OCF negative in FY24 (-180 Cr) and barely positive in FY25 (+27 Cr) — this is a cash-consuming, not cash-generating, business despite reported profits
Total assets doubled in one year (INR 1,644 → 3,373 Cr) alongside equity surge (INR 424 → 1,587 Cr) suggesting a large capital raise that dilutes future returns
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Invert first, as I always do: what could go catastrophically wrong? Almost everything here. The FY25 net profit of INR 351 Cr is a mirage — INR 259 Cr came from "Other Income," likely a one-time asset sale or investment gain. Strip that away, apply a reasonable tax rate, and core earnings are approximately INR 70-100 Cr. The market cap of INR 26,673 Cr then implies 260-380x real earnings. The cash flow statement confirms this: a business generating INR 3,112 Cr in revenue and INR 248 Cr in operating income should throw off real cash — instead it produced INR 27 Cr OCF and INR 1 Cr FCF in FY25. The working capital cycle is consuming every rupee of operating profit, which is what you'd expect from a hardware distributor with inventory and receivable bloat.

The underlying business has genuine merits — CP PLUS is the dominant domestic brand in an INR 10,000+ Cr surveillance market growing at 15%+ annually, with government mandates (Smart Cities, CCTNS) providing structural demand. ROE of 20.9% and ROCE of 19.5% look acceptable on the surface. But these returns are on an equity base just inflated by the one-time income event, and ROIC on the core operating business — given the working capital intensity — is likely in the 12-15% range at best. For a hardware-heavy, Chinese-competition-exposed, zero-FCF business, an EV/EBITDA of 68.76x is not a price I will pay. The promoter's 76.91% holding is good for alignment, but the opaque "Other Income" spike demands explanation before any capital commitment.
